incident_description: We installed a Frigidaire 5 burner LP cooktop, model FFGC3626SSE,  in our new home October 23, 2019 and began using the cooktop November 1, 2019.  After a month of use we noticed that the stems of the plastic control knobs were cracking.  Upon further inspection, we noted that all 5 control knobs were cracked to a degree.  The problem became so serious that the metal clip inside the plastic stem was no longer held in place and would spin independently of the knob.  My wife called me at work around January 15, 2020 because she could not get a burner to turn off due to the control knob spinning freely.  The plastic stem held long enough to turn the burner on but failed when my wife attempted to shut the burner down.  Had the knob been turned past the ignition position allowing gas to flow without igniting and then failed, the result could have been an explosion.  As a stopgap, I tightly wound the plastic stems with electrical tape to control the cracking and then called Frigidaire customer service.  Frigidaire agreed to send 5 new control knobs which were the same style as the original.  We received a package of the new burner knobs around January 25, 2020 (the packing label was dated 1/23/20) and began replacing the knobs that were critical.  Within a couple of weeks, the new knobs began to crack as well
